stem: low + (high - low) / 2 instead of (low + high) / 2 because:
options: low + high can OVERFLOW int on huge arrays - a real bug that sat in the JDK for years
explanation: Same value, no overflow. Free insurance - write it by habit.

stem: The loop must be while (low <= high), not <, because:
options: A ONE-ITEM range (low == high) is still searchable - < would skip it
explanation: One of binary search's three classic off-by-ones; the others are moving to middle±1 and adapting bounds for variants.

stem: ONE search of unsorted data: sort-then-binary or just linear?
options: LINEAR - sorting costs O(n log n), more than the O(n) single search it would save
explanation: Sort pays off across MANY searches. Many lookups by key? A Dictionary beats even binary search (3.2).

stem: "Guess my number 1-100, I say higher/lower" is beatable in at most:
options: 7 - ceil(log2 100), binary search as a strategy
explanation: Higher/lower IS the comparison; halving the range is optimal play. Project 7.1 proves it empirically over all 100 secrets.

stem: Setting high = middle (instead of middle - 1) risks:
options: An INFINITE LOOP - a two-item range can stop shrinking
explanation: If middle rounds to low, the range never narrows. The middle is already checked - exclude it on both sides.
